title: Normal Light Load
description: Standard low-utilization scenario where the server easily manages arrival flow.
notes: Utilization is 50%. On average, 1 customer in system (0.5 in queue, 0.5 at server). Lw = 2.0.

title: Moderate Load
description: Realistic everyday operating scenario with moderate customer presence.
notes: Utilization is 60%. Average time in system is 0.50 hours (30 min), queue wait is 0.30 hours (18 min). Lw = 2.5.

title: High Congestion (Near Peak)
description: Peak hour scenario testing high utilization and non-linear queue buildup.
notes: Utilization is 80%. System empty only 20% of the time. Average queue length increases to 3.2 customers. Lw = 5.0.

title: Fractional / Decimal Rates
description: Low-frequency arrival and service rates validating decimal input precision.
notes: Arrival every 2 hours, service takes 40 minutes (2/3 hr). System remains clear 66.7% of time. Lw = 1.5.

title: Critical Boundary (λ = μ)
description: Edge case where arrival rate equals service capacity, rendering the system unstable.

expected.warning: System is unstable (λ ≥ μ). Utilization reaches 100%, queue length grows infinitely without equilibrium.

notes: Queue size variance is infinite; no steady-state probability distribution exists.

title: Severe Overload (λ > μ)
description: Arrival rate strictly surpasses service rate, causing permanent queue buildup.

expected.warning: System is severely overloaded (λ > μ, ρ = 1.50). Service capacity cannot cope with incoming flow.

notes: Deterministic queue growth at rate of (12 - 8) = 4 customers per time unit.

title: Invalid Input: Negative Arrival Rate
description: Validation test for strictly positive parameter requirements (λ ≤ 0).

expected.error: Arrival rate (λ) must be a positive real number greater than 0.

notes: Arrival rate represents physical arrival frequency and cannot be negative or zero.

title: Invalid Input: Zero Service Rate
description: Validation test for division by zero and non-positive service capacity (μ ≤ 0).

expected.error: Service rate (μ) must be a positive real number greater than 0.

notes: Zero service rate implies dead service channel with infinite backlog.
